claim: ME31B, Trailer Hitch (TRAL), and Cup are maternally deposited Drosophila RNA-binding proteins that are cleared during the maternal-to-zygotic transition (MZT).
source: we previously found that three maternally deposited Drosophila RNA-binding proteins (ME31B, Trailer Hitch [TRAL], and Cup) are also cleared during the MZT by unknown mechanisms.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and introduction, referencing previous work (Wang et al., 2017).

claim: ME31B, TRAL, and Cup are degraded by the ubiquitin-proteasome system.
source: Here, we show that these proteins are degraded by the ubiquitin-proteasome system.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data showing ubiquitination and proteasome dependence.

claim: Marie Kondo (an E2 conjugating enzyme) is required for the destruction of ME31B, TRAL, and Cup.
source: Marie Kondo, an E2 conjugating enzyme, and the E3 CTLH ligase are required for the destruction of ME31B, TRAL, and Cup.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by RNAi knockdown experiments showing stabilization of these proteins.

claim: The E3 CTLH ligase is required for the destruction of ME31B, TRAL, and Cup.
source: Marie Kondo, an E2 conjugating enzyme, and the E3 CTLH ligase are required for the destruction of ME31B, TRAL, and Cup.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by RNAi knockdown experiments and immunoprecipitation data.

claim: The Drosophila CTLH complex has a different substrate recognition mechanism than orthologous complexes.
source: Structure modeling of the Drosophila CTLH complex suggests that substrate recognition is different than orthologous complexes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by structural modeling comparisons with yeast and human complexes.

claim: Egg activation mediates clearance of ME31B, TRAL, and Cup through the Pan Gu kinase.
source: Despite occurring hours earlier, egg activation mediates clearance of these proteins through the Pan Gu kinase, which stimulates translation of Kdo mRNA.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experiments in png mutants and translational profiling data.

claim: Pan Gu kinase stimulates translation of Kdo mRNA.
source: Despite occurring hours earlier, egg activation mediates clearance of these proteins through the Pan Gu kinase, which stimulates translation of Kdo mRNA.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by ribosome profiling data showing PNG-dependent translational upregulation.

claim: ME31B, TRAL, and Cup form a complex that blocks translation initiation.
source: ME31B, TRAL, and Cup form a complex that blocks translation initiation (Kinkelin et al., 2012; Nakamura et al., 2004; Nelson et al., 2004; Wilhelm et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with multiple supporting citations.

claim: ME31B, TRAL, and Cup are required for oogenesis.
source: All three proteins are required for oogenesis, and they appear to bind and repress thousands of deposited maternal mRNAs (Keyes and Spradling, 1997; Nakamura et al., 2001; Tritschler et al., 2008; Wang et al., 2017; Wilhelm et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: ME31B, TRAL, and Cup bind and repress thousands of deposited maternal mRNAs.
source: All three proteins are required for oogenesis, and they appear to bind and repress thousands of deposited maternal mRNAs (Keyes and Spradling, 1997; Nakamura et al., 2001; Tritschler et al., 2008; Wang et al., 2017; Wilhelm et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The degradation of ME31B, TRAL, and Cup coincides with the major wave of zygotic transcription.
source: Recently, we found that three RNA-binding proteins (ME31B, Trailer Hitch [TRAL], and Cup) are rapidly degraded during the MZT in Drosophila melanogaster, at a time point coinciding with the major wave of zygotic transcription (Wang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: The PNG kinase is composed of three subunits: PNG, Giant Nuclei (GNU), and Plutonium (PLU).
source: Composed of three subunits (PNG, Giant Nuclei [GNU], and Plutonium [PLU]), the PNG kinase is central to the oocyte-to-egg transition and mediates key aspects of embryogenesis, including resumption of the cell cycle, zygotic transcription, and maternal mRNA clearance (Elfring et al., 1997; Tadros et al., 2007; Vardy and Orr-Weaver, 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The PNG kinase is central to the oocyte-to-egg transition and mediates key aspects of embryogenesis, including resumption of the cell cycle, zygotic transcription, and maternal mRNA clearance.
source: Composed of three subunits (PNG, Giant Nuclei [GNU], and Plutonium [PLU]), the PNG kinase is central to the oocyte-to-egg transition and mediates key aspects of embryogenesis, including resumption of the cell cycle, zygotic transcription, and maternal mRNA clearance (Elfring et al., 1997; Tadros et al., 2007; Vardy and Orr-Weaver, 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The oocyte-to-egg transition in Drosophila does not require fertilization but is instead triggered by egg activation.
source: Unlike many animals, the oocyte-to-egg transition in Drosophila does not require fertilization but is instead triggered by egg activation (Doane, 1960; Heifetz et al., 2001; Horner and Wolfner, 2008a).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The PNG kinase is activated by mechanical stress as the oocyte passes through the oviduct.
source: Here, the PNG kinase is activated by mechanical stress as the oocyte passes through the oviduct, and then phosphorylation and degradation of the GNU subunit quickly inactivates the kinase, restricting its activity to the first half hour after egg activation (Hara et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Phosphorylation and degradation of the GNU subunit quickly inactivates the PNG kinase, restricting its activity to the first half hour after egg activation.
source: Here, the PNG kinase is activated by mechanical stress as the oocyte passes through the oviduct, and then phosphorylation and degradation of the GNU subunit quickly inactivates the kinase, restricting its activity to the first half hour after egg activation (Hara et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: PNG activity leads to changes in the poly(A)-tail length and translation of thousands of transcripts during egg activation.
source: Possibly by phosphorylating key RNA-binding proteins such as Pumilio, PNG activity leads to changes in the poly(A)-tail length and translation of thousands of transcripts during egg activation (Hara et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: The PNG kinase phosphorylates ME31B, Cup, and TRAL.
source: The PNG kinase also phosphorylates ME31B, Cup, and TRAL (Hara et al., 2018), but it is unclear what effect phosphorylation has on these proteins.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: ME31B-GFP robustly decreased from 2 to 3 hr after egg laying in control embryos.
source: Consistent with western blotting, the GFP signal in control (png50/FM7) embryos robustly decreased from 2 to 3 hr after egg laying (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1A,B.

claim: The GFP signal remained constant through 2-3 hr after egg laying in png50/png50 embryos.
source: In contrast, the GFP signal remained constant through this time period in png50/png50 embryos (hereafter referred to as png50), consistent with our previous study (Wang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1A,B, with reference to previous work.

claim: GNU is required for the destruction of ME31B.
source: When either GNU or PLU were knocked down (Figure 1C,D), ME31B-GFP was again stabilized, thus confirming that its destruction requires the full PNG kinase.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: PLU is required for the destruction of ME31B.
source: When either GNU or PLU were knocked down (Figure 1C,D), ME31B-GFP was again stabilized, thus confirming that its destruction requires the full PNG kinase.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: ME31B-GFP was unstable in activated, but unfertilized, eggs.
source: In contrast to our results in png50 embryos, ME31B-GFP was still unstable in the activated, but unfertilized, eggs.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Degradation of ME31B is triggered by egg activation through PNG activity.
source: Taken together, we conclude that degradation of ME31B is triggered by egg activation through PNG activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experiments showing PNG dependence and fertilization independence.

claim: ME31B is ubiquitinated.
source: An ubiquitin smear was detected in immunoprecipitants by western blotting at a size consistent with polyubiquitinated ME31B-GFP (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Ubiquitination of ME31B depends upon the PNG kinase activity.
source: This ubiquitination was not detectable in png50 mutant embryos and thus depended upon the PNG kinase activity (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: ME31B-GFP is not degraded by autophagy.
source: Knockdown of five autophagy components, such as Atg4a or Atg8a, gave viable embryos. However, ME31B-GFP was not stabilized in any of these knockdown embryos; indeed, in some cases, it appeared to be degraded more quickly than in the control embryos (Figure 2B, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Depleting the proteasome partially stabilizes ME31B-GFP.
source: Importantly, we observed partial stabilization of ME31B-GFP in both knockdown embryos (Figure 2C–E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2C-E for Rpn10 and Rpn11 knockdowns.

claim: UBC-E2H/Marie Kondo is an E2 ligase conserved from yeast to humans.
source: Although our initial E3 screen failed to reveal any strong candidates, knockdown of UBC-E2H, an E2 ligase conserved from yeast to humans (Kaiser et al., 1995; Kaiser et al., 1994; Lampert et al., 2018), blocked degradation of ME31B-GFP and nearly phenocopied the dynamics seen in png50 mutants (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the results with supporting citations.

claim: Knockdown of UBC-E2H blocked degradation of ME31B-GFP and nearly phenocopied the dynamics seen in png50 mutants.
source: Although our initial E3 screen failed to reveal any strong candidates, knockdown of UBC-E2H, an E2 ligase conserved from yeast to humans (Kaiser et al., 1995; Kaiser et al., 1994; Lampert et al., 2018), blocked degradation of ME31B-GFP and nearly phenocopied the dynamics seen in png50 mutants (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Both wild-type ME31B and ME31B-GFP fusion proteins were stabilized when UBC-E2H was depleted.
source: Because the maternal line contains both the wild-type and trap ME31B alleles, this experiment revealed that both wild-type and GFP fusion proteins were stabilized when UBC-E2H was depleted (Figure 3C), albeit more so for the fusion protein than wild-type one.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Endogenous, untagged Cup and TRAL were stabilized in the UBC-E2H knockdown embryos.
source: Importantly, as determined by western blotting, endogenous, untagged Cup and TRAL were also stabilized in the UBC-E2H knockdown embryos (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Ubiquitination of ME31B-GFP was undetectable in Kdo knockdown embryos.
source: Finally, through immunoprecipitation experiments, we determined that ubiquitination of ME31B-GFP was undetectable in Kdo knockdown embryos (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Kdo is conserved from yeast to humans and is known to work through the CTLH E3 ligase.
source: Kdo is conserved from yeast to humans and is known to work through the CTLH E3 ligase, a multicomponent complex (Lampert et al., 2018; Santt et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the results with supporting citations.

claim: The Drosophila CTLH complex includes RanBPM, Muskelin, CG3295, CG7611, CG6617, and CG31357 as putative homologs of human CTLH components.
source: Using BLAST for the human CTLH components, we were easily able to identify putative D. melanogaster homologs: RanBPM (homologous to Hs RanBP9), Muskelin, CG3295 (homologous to Hs RMND5A/GID2), CG7611 (homologous to Hs WDR26), CG6617 (homologous to Hs TWA1/GID8), and CG31357 (homologous to Hs MAEA) (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Muskelin, RanBPM, and CG6617 were identified in all four ME31B-GFP and Cup-GFP immunoprecipitation samples.
source: Consistent with our previous work (Wang et al., 2017), both immunoprecipitations readily pulled-down other members of the Cup–TRAL–ME31B complex. We were able to identify Muskelin, RanBPM, and CG6617 in all four samples.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4B,C.

claim: CG3295 was detected in both ME31B-GFP pull-downs and one Cup-GFP pull-down.
source: We also detected CG3295 in both ME31B-GFP pull-downs and one Cup-GFP pull-down, and CG31357 in both ME31B-GFP pull-downs.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4B,C.

claim: CG31357 was detected in both ME31B-GFP pull-downs.
source: We also detected CG3295 in both ME31B-GFP pull-downs and one Cup-GFP pull-down, and CG31357 in both ME31B-GFP pull-downs.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Depletion of CG3295, Muskelin, or RanBPM almost completely stabilized ME31B-GFP.
source: In contrast to what we had observed with other E3 ligases (Figure 2—source data 1), depletion of CG3295, Muskelin, or RanBPM almost completely stabilized ME31B-GFP.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4D.

claim: RNAi directed against CG7611 did not affect the destruction of ME31B.
source: RNAi directed against CG7611, the one component that we failed to detect by mass spectrometry, did not affect the destruction of ME31B, although we cannot exclude the possibility that CG7611 protein levels were not sufficiently affected.
evidence: This is stated in the results.

claim: ME31B, Cup and TRAL were stabilized when the CTLH complex was depleted.
source: Consistent with these results, when we used western blotting to look at levels of ME31B, Cup and TRAL, we found that all were stabilized when the CTLH complex was depleted (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Kdo levels were unaffected in CTLH complex knockdown embryos.
source: However, as determined by western blotting, Kdo levels were unaffected in these knockdown embryos (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: RanBPM was detected in ME31B-GFP immunoprecipitations.
source: Consistent with our mass spectrometry analysis (Figure 4B), we detected RanBPM in ME31B-GFP immunoprecipitations (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The Drosophila CTLH E3 ligase is at least composed of RanBPM, Muskelin, CG6617, CG3295, and CG31357.
source: Taken together, we conclude that the CTLH E3 ligase is required for the destruction of ME31B, Cup, and TRAL, and, in the early Drosophila embryo, is at least composed of RanBPM, Muskelin, CG6617, CG3295, and CG31357, although the role of CG7611 remains unknown.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the immunoprecipitation and knockdown experiments.

claim: The yeast Gid complex is composed of three sections: a catalytic module made by Gid2 and Gid9; a scaffold of Gid8, Gid1, and Gid5; and a substrate adaptor module formed by Gid4.
source: The Gid complex is composed of three sections: a catalytic module made by Gid2 and Gid9; a scaffold of Gid8, Gid1, and Gid5; and a substrate adaptor module formed by Gid4 (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the results based on the cryoEM structure from Qiao et al., 2020.

claim: Kaz and Sou likely form the catalytic module of the Drosophila CTLH complex.
source: By analogy, we were able to assign roles to the known Drosophila components: Kaz and Sou likely form the catalytic module, while RanBPM and Hou are part of the scaffold domain (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the results based on homology to the yeast complex.

claim: RanBPM and Hou are part of the scaffold domain of the Drosophila CTLH complex.
source: By analogy, we were able to assign roles to the known Drosophila components: Kaz and Sou likely form the catalytic module, while RanBPM and Hou are part of the scaffold domain (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the results based on homology to the yeast complex.

claim: The interaction between RanBPM and ME31B-GFP was unaffected when Sou was depleted.
source: Consistent with such organization, when Sou was depleted, the interaction between RanBPM and ME31B-GFP was unaffected (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The interaction between RanBPM and ME31B-GFP depends upon Muskelin.
source: The interaction between RanBPM and ME31B-GFP did, however, depend upon Muskelin (Figure 5B), but with current structures, it is unclear how Muskelin interacts with the other components of the Drosophila CTLH complex.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5B.

claim: RanBPM lacks the Gid4-interacting loop present in yeast Gid1.
source: First, in S. cerevisiae, Gid4 makes the majority of its contacts only with Gid5. Nonetheless, one loop in Gid1 extends out to interact with Gid4 (Qiao et al., 2020). In contrast, no such loop is predicted in Drosophila RanBPM, although the flanking β sheet strands appear to exist (Figure 5D, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Houki lacks the Gid5-interacting tail present in yeast Gid8.
source: Second, in S. cerevisiae, the scaffold module is composed of Gid1, Gid5, and Gid8. Here, most of the Gid8 C-terminus wraps around Gid5 and makes nearly all of the interactions with Gid5. This domain appears to be also absent from Drosophila Hou, despite structural similarity in the rest of the protein (Figure 5E; Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5E and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Substrate recognition is likely different for the Drosophila CTLH complex than in other organisms.
source: Taken together, these analyses suggest that substrate recognition is likely different for the Drosophila CTLH complex than in other organisms and leaves open the question of how ME31B, Cup, and TRAL bind the E3 ligase.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the structural modeling analyses.

claim: The interaction between RanBPM and ME31B-GFP was unaffected by Kdo depletion.
source: Consistent with a role for the E3 ligase binding a target protein, interaction between RanBPM and ME31B-GFP was unaffected by Kdo depletion (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The interaction between RanBPM and ME31B-GFP remained robust in png50 embryos.
source: However, the interaction between RanBPM and ME31B-GFP remained robust in png50 embryos (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6B.

claim: An interaction between endogenous Cup and RanBPM was detected in both wild-type and png50 embryos.
source: Similarly, when we immunoprecipitated endogenous Cup, we were able to detect an interaction with RanBPM in both wild-type and png50 embryos (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6C.

claim: PNG activity is not required for the CTLH complex to recognize and interact with ME31B and Cup.
source: Thus, we conclude that PNG activity is not required for the CTLH complex to recognize and interact with ME31B and Cup.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the immunoprecipitation experiments in png50 embryos.

claim: Translation of Kdo mRNA was repressed through oogenesis.
source: In contrast, the most striking change occurred for translation of Kdo mRNA: although translation of Kdo mRNA was repressed through oogenesis, its translation increased 25-fold during the oocyte-to-embryo transition (Figure 7A), placing it in the top 10% of genes upregulated at this developmental transition.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7A using ribosome profiling data.

claim: Translation of Kdo mRNA increased 25-fold during the oocyte-to-embryo transition.
source: In contrast, the most striking change occurred for translation of Kdo mRNA: although translation of Kdo mRNA was repressed through oogenesis, its translation increased 25-fold during the oocyte-to-embryo transition (Figure 7A), placing it in the top 10% of genes upregulated at this developmental transition.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7A using ribosome profiling data.

claim: Kdo was not translationally upregulated in png50-activated embryos.
source: However, Kdo was not translationally upregulated in png50-activated embryos (Figure 7B), and its translation differed by more than 200-fold between wild-type and mutant-activated eggs.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7B using ribosome profiling data.

claim: Kdo translation differed by more than 200-fold between wild-type and png50 mutant-activated eggs.
source: However, Kdo was not translationally upregulated in png50-activated embryos (Figure 7B), and its translation differed by more than 200-fold between wild-type and mutant-activated eggs.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7B,C using ribosome profiling data.

claim: A dramatic increase in Kdo protein levels was detected over the first 3 hr of embryogenesis in wild-type embryos.
source: Consistent with this analysis, when we probed Kdo protein levels, we were able to detect a dramatic increase in protein levels over the first 3 hr of embryogenesis in wild-type embryos, but we were unable to detect expression at any time point in png50 mutant embryos (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Kdo protein expression was undetectable at any time point in png50 mutant embryos.
source: Consistent with this analysis, when we probed Kdo protein levels, we were able to detect a dramatic increase in protein levels over the first 3 hr of embryogenesis in wild-type embryos, but we were unable to detect expression at any time point in png50 mutant embryos (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7D.

claim: The poly(A) tail length on Kdo mRNA doubled upon egg activation in a manner dependent on PNG.
source: Pointing to a role of post-transcriptional gene regulation, the poly(A) tail length on Kdo mRNA also doubled upon egg activation in a manner dependent on PNG. This result suggests that the translational increase is partially mediated by an increase in poly(A)-tail length (Figure 7E,F), which directly impacts translational changes during egg activation (Eichhorn et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7E,F.

claim: ME31B binding changes during egg activation in a manner dependent on the PNG kinase.
source: These data indicate that although ME31B binds broadly similar transcripts in the oocyte and embryo, its binding does change at egg activation in a manner dependent on the PNG kinase.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7H,I using RNA immunoprecipitation data.

claim: The change in ME31B-GFP binding at egg activation was strongly correlated with the change in translational efficiency.
source: Moreover, we found that the change in ME31B-GFP binding at egg activation was strongly correlated with the change in translational efficiency (rs = –0.48, p<10–15) such that those mRNAs with diminished ME31B-GFP binding were translationally activated and those with increased binding were translationally repressed (Figure 7J).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7J.

claim: ME31B-GFP binding to Kdo mRNA was substantially reduced upon egg activation in a PNG-dependent manner.
source: Importantly, as with poly(A)-tail length, ME31B-GFP binding to Kdo mRNA also changed upon egg activation and was substantially reduced in a PNG-dependent manner (Figure 7H,I).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7H,I.

claim: During oogenesis, ME31B acts to repress translation of Kdo mRNA.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that, during oogenesis, ME31B, presumably via Cup and TRAL, acts to repress translation of Kdo mRNA and thus suppress production of its own E2.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the ME31B binding and translational efficiency data.

claim: Upon egg activation, PNG activity leads to extension of the Kdo mRNA poly(A) tail and stimulates the dissociation of ME31B from the transcript.
source: Upon egg activation, PNG activity not only leads to extension of the Kdo mRNA poly(A) tail, but also stimulates the dissociation of ME31B from the transcript.
evidence: This is stated in the results based on poly(A) tail length and ME31B binding data.

claim: Egg activation through PNG mediates translation upregulation of Kdo and leads to ME31B, Cup, and TRAL destruction.
source: Together, these two activities likely promote translation of Kdo, setting the stage for clearance of deposited ME31B, TRAL, and Cup.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined data on PNG, Kdo translation, and protein degradation.

claim: Degradation of ME31B, TRAL, and Cup is triggered by egg activation through the activity of the PNG kinase and appears to be mediated by the ubiquitin-proteasome system.
source: ME31B, Cup, and TRAL are RNA-binding proteins that are degraded during the MZT. Despite occurring several hours after egg laying, degradation of these proteins is triggered by egg activation through the activity of the PNG kinase and appears to be mediated by the ubiquitin-proteasome system (Figures 1 and 2).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion summarizing the results.

claim: Muskelin shows exquisite tissue-specificity and is only strongly expressed in the ovaries.
source: Interestingly, based on RNA-seq data from FlyBase (FlyBase Consortium et al., 2019), Muskelin shows exquisite tissue-specificity and is only strongly expressed in the ovaries.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation to FlyBase data.

claim: The list of proteins degraded during the Drosophila MZT includes GNU, Matrimony, Cort, Smaug, ME31B, TRAL, and Cup.
source: Over the past few years, the list of proteins degraded during the Drosophila MZT has grown and now includes GNU, Matrimony, Cort, Smaug, ME31B, TRAL, and Cup (Benoit et al., 2009; Hara et al., 2017; Pesin and Orr-Weaver, 2007; Wang et al., 2017; Whitfield et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with supporting citations.

claim: Unbiased mass spectrometry experiments suggest that Wispy and Dhd are robustly degraded during the MZT.
source: Unbiased mass spectrometry experiments also suggest that Wispy and Dhd are also robustly degraded (Sysoev et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: The maternal-to-zygotic transition (MZT) is a conserved step in animal development where control is passed from the maternal to the zygotic genome.
source: The maternal-to-zygotic transition (MZT) is a conserved step in animal development, where control is passed from the maternal to the zygotic genome.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract.

claim: The MZT requires both the activation of zygotic transcription and clearance of maternal transcripts.
source: Thus, the MZT requires both the activation of zygotic transcription and clearance of maternal transcripts.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction.

claim: Failure to mediate either activation of zygotic transcription or clearance of maternal transcripts is lethal for the embryo.
source: Failure to mediate either of these processes is lethal for the embryo (Benoit et al., 2009; Liang et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The ubiquitin-proteasome system is a major protein degradation pathway.
source: The ubiquitin-proteasome system is a major protein degradation pathway.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction.

claim: E3 ligases are typically thought to recognize target proteins, while E2 conjugating enzymes provide the activated ubiquitin and recognize the E3 ligase.
source: E3 ligases are typically thought to recognize target proteins, while E2 conjugating enzymes provide the activated ubiquitin and in turn recognize the E3 ligase (Komander and Rape, 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: There are hundreds of different E3 ligases and 29 annotated E2 conjugating enzymes in Drosophila.
source: There are hundreds of different E3 ligases and 29 annotated E2 conjugating enzymes in Drosophila (Du et al., 2011), but most of the client substrates are unknown, and few have been implicated in the MZT.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: PNG phosphorylation may contribute to the MZT by modulating the activities of ME31B, TRAL, and Cup, rather than their stability.
source: It is tempting to speculate that phosphorylation may then contribute to the MZT by modulating the activities of ME31B, TRAL, and Cup, rather than their stability.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation.

claim: The 3'UTR of Kdo contains several putative Pumilio-binding sites.
source: One hint may be that the 3'UTR of Kdo contains several putative Pumilio-binding sites, and translation of Kdo is upregulated in ovaries where Pumilio has been knocked down (Flora et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: Translation of Kdo is upregulated in ovaries where Pumilio has been knocked down.
source: One hint may be that the 3'UTR of Kdo contains several putative Pumilio-binding sites, and translation of Kdo is upregulated in ovaries where Pumilio has been knocked down (Flora et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: Pumilio is a target of PNG.
source: Pumilio is also a target of PNG (Hara et al., 2018), and so a possible model is that translational repressors, such as Pumilio, are phosphorylated and inactivated at egg activation, leading to the production of Kdo.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: PNG mediates the translational upregulation of Zelda and Smaug, key MZT effectors.
source: PNG also mediates the translational upregulation of key MZT effectors: Zelda, the pioneer transcription factor, and Smaug, an RNA-binding protein that targets nearly two-thirds of the maternal transcriptome for degradation (Chen et al., 2014; Eichhorn et al., 2016; Tadros et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with supporting citations.

claim: Smaug targets nearly two-thirds of the maternal transcriptome for degradation.
source: PNG also mediates the translational upregulation of key MZT effectors: Zelda, the pioneer transcription factor, and Smaug, an RNA-binding protein that targets nearly two-thirds of the maternal transcriptome for degradation (Chen et al., 2014; Eichhorn et al., 2016; Tadros et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with supporting citations.

claim: Egg activation stimulates the production of multiple key factors that are important for clearing the maternal RNA and protein dowry and for producing zygotic gene products.
source: Together with our results, a picture is emerging that egg activation stimulates the production of multiple key factors that are important for clearing the maternal RNA and protein dowry and for producing zygotic gene products.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a synthesis of the findings.

claim: Clearance of the maternal protein dowry appears to be a coordinated, but as-yet underappreciated, aspect of the MZT.
source: Clearance of the maternal protein dowry thus appears to be a coordinated, but as-yet underappreciated, aspect of the MZT.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a conclusion.

claim: ME31B-GFP is expressed from the endogenous locus and recapitulates the dynamics of the wild-type protein.
source: To do so, we took advantage of an ME31B-GFP trap line where the fusion protein is expressed from the endogenous locus (Buszczak et al., 2007); we have previously shown that ME31B-GFP recapitulates the dynamics of the wild-type protein (Wang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the results with supporting citations.

claim: Injection of MG132 into embryos stabilized endogenous ME31B, TRAL, and Cup.
source: The role of the proteasome in degrading ME31B is consistent with results from a complementary study where injection of MG132 into embryos stabilized endogenous ME31B, TRAL, and Cup (Cao et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the results with a supporting citation.

claim: Similar results to the ME31B-CTLH complex interaction were seen in previous studies of ME31B complexes in embryonic lysates.
source: Similar results were seen in previous studies of ME31B complexes in embryonic lysates (Götze et al., 2017) and in a complimentary study (Cao et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the results with supporting citations.

claim: The translational increase of Kdo is partially mediated by an increase in poly(A)-tail length.
source: This result suggests that the translational increase is partially mediated by an increase in poly(A)-tail length (Figure 7E,F), which directly impacts translational changes during egg activation (Eichhorn et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the results with a supporting citation and shown in Figure 7E,F.

claim: Changes in poly(A)-tail length directly impact translational changes during egg activation.
source: This result suggests that the translational increase is partially mediated by an increase in poly(A)-tail length (Figure 7E,F), which directly impacts translational changes during egg activation (Eichhorn et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the results with a supporting citation.

claim: ME31B is broadly associated with translational repression in the early embryo.
source: Because we had previously found that ME31B is broadly associated with translational repression in the early embryo (Wang et al., 2017), we wondered if ME31B binding might also change during egg activation and if such changes could impact translation.
evidence: This is stated in the results with a supporting citation.

claim: ME31B-GFP binding in stage 14 oocytes was highly correlated with that measured previously in 0–1 hr wild-type embryos.
source: Although ME31B-GFP binding in stage 14 oocytes was highly correlated with that measured previously in 0–1 hr wild-type embryos (Spearman r [rs]=0.66, p<10–15), its binding was even more similar in 0–1 hr png50 embryos (rs = 0.84, p<10–15; Fisher's r-to-z transformation: p<10–15; Figure 7H,I).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7H,I.

claim: ME31B-GFP binding in stage 14 oocytes was even more similar in 0–1 hr png50 embryos than in wild-type embryos.
source: Although ME31B-GFP binding in stage 14 oocytes was highly correlated with that measured previously in 0–1 hr wild-type embryos (Spearman r [rs]=0.66, p<10–15), its binding was even more similar in 0–1 hr png50 embryos (rs = 0.84, p<10–15; Fisher's r-to-z transformation: p<10–15; Figure 7H,I).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7H,I.

claim: mRNAs with diminished ME31B-GFP binding were translationally activated and those with increased binding were translationally repressed.
source: Moreover, we found that the change in ME31B-GFP binding at egg activation was strongly correlated with the change in translational efficiency (rs = –0.48, p<10–15) such that those mRNAs with diminished ME31B-GFP binding were translationally activated and those with increased binding were translationally repressed (Figure 7J).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7J.

claim: The relationship between ME31B binding changes and translational efficiency changes held even after controlling for changes in poly(A)-tail length.
source: Importantly, this relationship held even after we controlled for changes in poly(A)-tail length (rs = –0.40, p<10–15).
evidence: This is stated in the results.

claim: PNG activity at egg activation triggers two independent mechanisms for altering translation: changing poly(A)-tail length and altering ME31B binding.
source: Thus, these analyses indicate that PNG activity at egg activation triggers two independent, albeit related, mechanisms for altering translation: changing poly(A)-tail length and altering ME31B binding.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from the data.

claim: Translational repressors, such as Pumilio, may be phosphorylated and inactivated at egg activation, leading to the production of Kdo.
source: Pumilio is also a target of PNG (Hara et al., 2018), and so a possible model is that translational repressors, such as Pumilio, are phosphorylated and inactivated at egg activation, leading to the production of Kdo.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a speculative model.

claim: PNG may contribute through other, as-yet undiscovered, mechanisms such as phosphorylating unknown CTLH adaptor proteins.
source: Although PNG may contribute through other, as-yet undiscovered, mechanisms as well (such as phosphorylating unknown CTLH adaptor proteins), this link is sufficient to explain the PNG requirement for ME31B degradation: in the absence of Kdo, ME31B is stable during the MZT, and in the absence of PNG, Kdo is not detectably expressed.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation.

claim: In the absence of Kdo, ME31B is stable during the MZT.
source: Although PNG may contribute through other, as-yet undiscovered, mechanisms as well (such as phosphorylating unknown CTLH adaptor proteins), this link is sufficient to explain the PNG requirement for ME31B degradation: in the absence of Kdo, ME31B is stable during the MZT, and in the absence of PNG, Kdo is not detectably expressed.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion summarizing the results.

claim: In the absence of PNG, Kdo is not detectably expressed.
source: Although PNG may contribute through other, as-yet undiscovered, mechanisms as well (such as phosphorylating unknown CTLH adaptor proteins), this link is sufficient to explain the PNG requirement for ME31B degradation: in the absence of Kdo, ME31B is stable during the MZT, and in the absence of PNG, Kdo is not detectably expressed.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion summarizing the results.

claim: The CTLH complex has not yet been studied in Drosophila prior to this work.
source: Although the CTLH complex is conserved, it has not yet been studied in Drosophila.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: Gid7 and WDR26 are important in the yeast and human CTLH complexes, respectively.
source: Although Gid7 and WDR26 are important in the yeast and human versions, respectively, and we identified a Drosophila ortholog (CG7611), we found no evidence of its association with ME31B or requirement for ME31B degradation; the role of CG7611 in the Drosophila CTLH complex warrants further investigation.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: Gid4 and Gid5 are critical for substrate recognition in S. cerevisiae.
source: We were also unable to identify orthologs of Gid4 and Gid5, which are critical for substrate recognition in S. cerevisiae (Lampert et al., 2018; Maitland et al., 2019; Santt et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with supporting citations.

claim: Phosphorylation by PNG may impact the ability of ME31B, TRAL, and Cup to repress gene expression.
source: Intriguing observations from the Orr-Weaver lab suggest that the modification can impact the ability of these proteins to repress gene expression (Hara et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: Translational control of Kdo may partly explain how ME31B, a ubiquitous protein, is specifically destabilized in the early embryo.
source: This observation, together with the translational control of Kdo, may partly explain how ME31B, a ubiquitous protein, is specifically destabilized in the early embryo.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an inference.

claim: Kdo was the seventh-most affected transcript in terms of PNG dependence.
source: In fact, Kdo was the seventh-most affected transcript (Figure 7C), showing a similar dependence on PNG as Smaug, which encodes a well-known and important downstream target of PNG activity.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Kdo shows a similar dependence on PNG as Smaug.
source: In fact, Kdo was the seventh-most affected transcript (Figure 7C), showing a similar dependence on PNG as Smaug, which encodes a well-known and important downstream target of PNG activity.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Known CTLH component mRNAs were either not affected or downregulated during egg activation.
source: Known CTLH component mRNAs were either not affected or downregulated during egg activation (Figure 7—figure supplement 1), although we cannot exclude the hypothesis that unidentified components may be regulated by PNG.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Kdo mRNA is in the top 10% of genes upregulated at the oocyte-to-embryo transition.
source: In contrast, the most striking change occurred for translation of Kdo mRNA: although translation of Kdo mRNA was repressed through oogenesis, its translation increased 25-fold during the oocyte-to-embryo transition (Figure 7A), placing it in the top 10% of genes upregulated at this developmental transition.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7A.
